note: Evidence, not an engine input -- parallel to house_district_panel.json but for U.S. Senate generals. Nothing in engine/ reads this file.

source.dataset: MIT Election Data and Science Lab (MEDSL), U.S. Senate constituency returns 1976-2018
source.upstream_source: Clerk of the U.S. House, "Statistics of the Congressional Election"; 2018 from state election offices

transform: Keep stage="gen" and special=FALSE. Group candidate rows by year+state (Senate races are statewide, no district).
Sum candidatevotes across party lines for the same candidate name (fusion voting -- NY in particular runs one candidate on 4-6 lines), name upper-cased and stripped to A-Z and spaces.

A candidate is D if ANY of its lines is democrat / democratic-farmer-labor / democratic-npl, R if ANY line is republican -- checked over the full set of a candidate's lines, not the first line encountered, since fusion candidates' major-party line is not always listed first. Candidates carrying both a D and an R line, or neither, are excluded from the two-party totals.
demName/repName: the normalized name of the top D/R candidate by summed votes, kept (unlike the House panel) so a later pass can name-match the same person across cycles rather than only the party.

inc: +1 if this state's senate race 6 years earlier (the same class, since regular Senate elections recur on a fixed 6-year cycle per class and no two classes in one state are up in the same year) was won by D, -1 if by R, 0 if there was no such race or it tied.
